regulator: Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority (TMDA) – https://www.tmda.go.tz

facts.title: Compendium of device guidelines (June 2024)
facts.body: TMDA's rules for devices, IVDs and lab equipment are in one Compendium (June 2024). It replaces the separate 2020 guidelines and covers procedure, technical documents, classification, clinical evidence, labelling, grouping, software and borderline products. Applications go through the TMDA Traders' Portal, in English or Kiswahili.

facts.title: Registration or notification
facts.body: Classes B, C and D, plus Class A devices that are sterile, active or measuring, need full registration. Other Class A devices only need notification, which is processed in 5 working days. TMDA can overrule the manufacturer's proposed class.

facts.title: Likely classes for our product types
facts.body: The Compendium itself says nasal sprays that hydrate the nasal passages and sinuses are Class B, while saline nasal solutions only for clearing or rinsing are Class A. Lubricant eye drops are usually Class B. OVDs are usually Class C, and intra-articular HA is usually Class C or D (absorbed, biological effect). Any device made from or with animal tissue or derivatives (e.g. animal-sourced HA) is Class D under Rule 14.

facts.title: No formal reliance route for devices
facts.body: The Compendium has no abridged or reliance pathway for devices; every registrable device gets a first and second assessment. Foreign approvals and marketing history are submitted as supporting evidence. We found no EAC joint-assessment route for devices.

facts.title: Target timelines
facts.body: Screening and invoicing take 1-2 working days. Scheduling takes up to 10 working days (A/B) or 20 (C/D), assessment 23 working days (A/B) or about 40 (C/D), quality review 5 or 8, and DG approval 5 or 25. That totals about 2 months for A/B and 4-5 months for C/D, not counting queries or site audits. Query responses are due within 60 working days or the file is treated as withdrawn.

facts.title: Registration fees (imported)
facts.body: Under the Fees and Charges Regulations 2022 (GN 686), imported devices cost USD 100 for Class A notification, USD 500 for registrable Class A, and USD 2,500 for Class B, C or D. TMDA's fee page still cited GN 686 in October 2026. Fees are non-refundable and paid via a control number after screening.

facts.title: Retention and variation fees
facts.body: Annual retention is USD 200 per registered device and USD 50 per notified device. A major variation costs USD 300 and a minor one USD 150. Changing the Local Technical Representative costs USD 2,000.

facts.title: GMP / quality audit fees
facts.body: A foreign GMP inspection or quality audit costs USD 4,000 (East Africa) to USD 7,500 (Americas, Australia) per block; Europe is USD 6,500 and Asia USD 6,000. Each extra production line or block costs up to 25% more.

facts.title: Local Responsible Person required
facts.body: A non-resident applicant must appoint a Local Responsible Person (also called authorised representative or local agent). It must be a company incorporated in Tanzania and licensed by TMDA to deal in medical devices. Proof of appointment goes with the application. The LRP handles market monitoring, recalls, user support and communication with TMDA.

facts.title: QMS audit as part of assessment
facts.body: A quality audit of the manufacturing site is part of the assessment, but its time is outside the target timelines. TMDA also accepts a desk assessment of GMP/QA for devices under a separate 2021 guideline. QMS certificates are needed for every design and manufacturing site, including contract manufacturers.

facts.title: Two commercial packs
facts.body: New applications and renewals for single-use and small devices need two commercial packs from the same batch, submitted after payment. Assessment does not start without samples. Large equipment can send photos and artwork instead.

facts.title: Shelf-life evidence
facts.body: Data must support the claimed shelf life on the label. Accelerated ageing can support the first claim if justified, but real-time results must follow when available. With no expiry date, TMDA treats the claim as an unlimited shelf life that must be justified.

facts.title: Technical documentation
facts.body: The dossier covers device details, a STED-style technical summary, Essential Principles and standards conformity, biocompatibility (ISO 10993), animal-origin materials, preclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing and sterilisation (SAL 10^-6), labelling, and a post-market surveillance plan and reports. Grouping as a family, system or group is allowed per application.

facts.title: Validity, renewal and PMS
facts.body: Registration is valid for 5 years and notification for 3 years. Renewal must be filed at least 90 days before expiry, with samples. Validity depends on paying annual retention, sending post-market surveillance reports twice a year and reporting adverse events.

facts.title: Import fee 2% of FOB
facts.body: Imports of medical devices and diagnostics pay a fee of 2% of FOB value under GN 686. Late payment carries a 15% penalty.

routes.label: Class A notification
routes.description: Notification for non-sterile, non-measuring, non-active Class A devices, such as rinse-only saline nasal spray.

routes.label: Class A registration
routes.description: Full registration for sterile, measuring or active Class A devices.

routes.label: Class B registration
routes.description: Full assessment, e.g. HA lubricant eye drops and hydrating nasal sprays.

routes.label: Class C registration
routes.description: Full assessment, e.g. OVDs and many intra-articular HA products.

routes.label: Class D registration
routes.description: Full assessment for high-risk devices, incl. any made with animal-derived materials.
